newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey presses drive against Kurd rebels in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Turkey presses drive against Kurd rebels in Iraq.

text.p: Turkey is pressing on with its six-week-old military campaign against Kurdish rebels in northern Iraq despite a partial pullout of its forces, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Monday.
The spokesman, quoted by the state-run Anatolian news agency, said some Turkish troops remained in northern Iraq in support of Iraqi Kurdish groups.

Sources at the main Iraqi border crossing at Habur say Turkey has withdrawn large numbers of armoured vehicles since last week, but said fresh troops had been sent in to replace soldiers pulled out of the region.

More than 10,000 Turkish soldiers poured across the border into northern Iraq from May 14 in an attempt to eliminate Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels from the region, which the guerrillas use as a base for raids into Turkey.
Turkey, allied with the region's Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), says the campaign has inflicted a "crushing blow" to the PKK.
"We have taken out the PKK, we have destroyed their infrastructure. We are making sure that they will never come back as a military group there," a KDP spokesman in Ankara told Reuters.
Turkey's assertion that the KDP invited Turkish troops into the region has not been confirmed by the KDP. "Turkish troops entered on their own agenda," the KDP spokesman said.
The spokesman accused the KDP's main Iraqi Kurd rivals, the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), of aiding the PKK, which is fighting for self-rule in southeast Turkey.

"The PKK have been assisted by the PUK so far eight times actually to come through the ceasefire line to attack to KDP positions...The PKK have formed small mobile groups with the assistance and participation of PUK," the KDP spokesman said.
A U.S.-brokered ceasefire last October ended months of fighting between the KDP and the PUK, who took over the U.N.-declared "safe haven" after the 1991 Gulf War.

"The PUK's position on this matter is clear. We totally deny supporting the PKK. This is just KDP propaganda to encourage the Turkish troops to attack the PUK," PUK spokesman Latif Rashid told Reuters.

The pro-rebel DEM news agency said on Monday that PKK forces launched Katyusha rockets at KDP positions near Rawanduz, killing eight KDP fighters. No PKK guerillas were killed in the attack, the agency said.
Turkey says it has killed more than 2,600 PKK fighters in the operation for the loss of 99 of its own soldiers and village guard militiamen.
Much of the Arab world and some of Turkey's Western allies have condemned Ankara for its foray the region.
The entire campaign has been carried out under a strict news blackout, with correspondents barred from the region and communications blocked, making independent confirmation of events impossible.
However, Western diplomats say the reported PKK death toll is exaggerated.
Turkey said on Monday it had killed 54 PKK guerillas inside Turkey in clashes over the last two days.
More than 24,000 people have been killed in the 12-year-old conflict between the Turkish security forces and the PKK.
